messages:
Jamie: Quick heads-up — saw a reproducible OOM on dedicated-us-east-2 with a long-context customer run (seq_length ~4096). flamegraph: https://artifacts/redwood/perf/2051234567/flame.svg
Jamie: Root cause looks like blockpool fragmentation after the rollout of the new fused-attn kernel; workspace per-request jumped ~1.8x in traces.
Sachin: Can you attach pprof + nvprof from the same run?
Jamie: pprof here: https://artifacts/redwood/perf/2051234567/pprof.pb.gz. nvprof shows a big peak at kernel `kv_streamer` and many small workspace allocs in allocator.cpp:482.
Maya: Did batching or routing policy change recently? I remember the dynamic-router flag toggled last week.
Natalie: Confirmed — routing.default_bias changed to favor latency which nudged kernel selection toward fused-attn-v2 for mid-length sequences. That reduces batching and increases per-request workspace usage.
Corey: Repro steps I ran locally: 
```sh
./bin/infer --model redwood/open-7b --kernel fused-attn-v2 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --trace nvprof --out trace.gz
```
perf-bot: :warning: Alert: OOM spike (prod-dedicated) 2051234567T00:12 — 8 failures in 5m
Sachin: Quick hypothesis: our aggressive compact-on-free compaction is creating lots of small fragments. With a higher workspace per-request there are fewer contiguous blocks for large windows.
Jamie: I compared allocator histograms pre/post-rollout. Pre-rollout ~90% of free space had contiguous runs >=64KB; post-rollout that dropped to ~37%.
Maya: Proposed mitigation: increase blockpool target for known large-window workloads and add a delayed/deferred compaction threshold keyed by recent window-size distribution.
Jamie: Sketch patch idea: 
```diff
- if (free_blocks < target) compact_immediately();
+ if (free_blocks < target && recent_large_windows_ratio > 0.2) compact_immediately();
+ else schedule_compaction(delay_ms=100);
```
Natalie: Also consider changing kernel routing to prefer the streaming kernel when seq > 2048 to reduce workspace usage, and keep fused for short, latency-sensitive queries.
Corey: A/B test locally with routing change + compaction-delay: OOMs went away in 200 trials. p95 latency for short queries up ~8ms, throughput improved overall.
Sachin: We should add counters: workspace_alloc_bytes, max_live_blocks, compaction_ops, recent_large_windows_ratio. Who can add these?
Jamie: I'll open a small PR that adds those counters and new config flags: `blockpool.compaction_delay_ms` and `routing.max_workspace_for_fused`.
Natalie: Rollout plan: feature-flag routing change, target canary hosts only, monitor p95 latency and token_cost.
ci-deploy-bot: Deploy queued: canary-group-3 with flag routing.fused_bias=0.3
Maya: One more note — KV cache compaction is particularly expensive with large KV sizes. We should decouple KV compaction from blockpool compaction so they can be tuned independently.
Corey: Agreed. Decoupling allowed us to keep cold KV compaction less frequent and only reclaim truly hot prefixes in local experiments.
Sachin: Action items:
1) Jamie: PR for counters + flags
2) Maya: implement delayed compaction policy
3) Natalie: orchestrate canary rollout + monitor dashboards
4) Corey: run perf harness for 10k iterations and share results
Jamie: Assigning tasks and will ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Perf test queued: blockpool-regression-harness-2051234567
ci-deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for canary-group-3 at 2051234575
Jamie: Thanks — will check dashboards in ~30m and report back.
